## Natural history notes

A small marsh skipper characterized by brown to orange-brown wings, pale spotting, and a compact body with the quick, low flight typical of skippers. In Florida, it is found mainly in coastal salt marshes, brackish marsh edges, tidal wetlands, and nearby grassy areas where its host grasses occur. Adults visit flowers for nectar and often perch low in marsh vegetation, while the caterpillars feed on marsh grasses, using folded or tied grass blades as protective shelters during development.
